pageTitle: Chorus Pedals: Bucket-Brigade Modulation, Spatial Stereo & 80s Shimmer
subtitle: The dimensional doubler — pitch modulation physics, LFO waveforms, true stereo spatial spread & iconic bucket-brigade circuits

introduction.title: Chorus Pedals: Bucket-Brigade Modulation, Spatial Stereo & 80s Shimmer
introduction.text:
Few guitar effects are as instantly recognizable or culturally defining as chorus. From the shimmering, crystalline arpeggios of Andy Summers on The Police's 'Message in a Bottle' and the moody post-punk soundscapes of The Cure, to the watery grunge roar of Kurt Cobain on 'Come As You Are' and the sparkling acoustic polish of 1980s pop ballads, chorus transforms a solitary, static guitar into an expansive, multi-layered acoustic ensemble.

The acoustic physics behind chorus is grounded in human vocal and instrumental ensembles. When a choir of vocalists or a section of violinists plays the exact same melody in unison, their notes are never mathematically identical: subtle, microtonal variations in pitch and timing create acoustic phase interference that the human ear perceives as lush, warm, and massive. A chorus pedal recreates this phenomenon electronically by splitting your guitar signal, delaying one copy by a tiny time window (typically 5ms to 25ms), modulating that delayed copy's pitch up and down using a Low-Frequency Oscillator (LFO), and recombining it with your dry guitar signal. When projected across a stereo pair of speakers, the dry and modulated waves cross in physical room air, enveloping the listener in breathtaking three-dimensional sound.
introduction.quote: Chorus takes a solitary, static guitar note and turns it into a shimmering ensemble. In stereo, it is not an electronic trick; it is two distinct acoustic sound waves crossing through the air to physically envelop the listener.

sections.title: How Chorus Works: The LFO & Delay Line Physics
sections.subtitle: The electronic mechanics of time-delay modulation and constructive phase interference

cards.title: The Anatomy of a Chorus Circuit
cards.description: A chorus pedal splits your guitar signal into two identical parallel paths: the 'Dry' path and the 'Wet' path. The wet path is sent into a specialized variable delay line (5ms to 25ms). A Low-Frequency Oscillator (LFO)—producing a smooth triangle or sine wave at sub-audible frequencies (typically 0.1Hz to 5Hz)—continually sweeps the delay time back and forth. Because changing delay time in real time alters playback speed, it introduces Doppler pitch-shifting (subtle vibrato). When this modulated wet signal is recombined with the unmodulated dry signal, phase cancellations create rolling comb-filter notches that sound like two guitarists playing in unison.

fields.label: Rate / Speed Knob
fields.value: Controls the frequency of the LFO (how rapidly the pitch sweeps up and down)

fields.label: Depth / Width Knob
fields.value: Controls the amplitude of the LFO sweep (how far the pitch deviates from the original note)

fields.label: Delay Time Window
fields.value: 5ms to 25ms (shorter than the human ear's 30ms echo threshold; perceived as doubling rather than slapback)

fields.label: Comb Filtering
fields.value: Continuous phase cancellations create rolling frequency dips that generate lush shimmer

items: Low Rate + High Depth creates a deep, slow, swimming, oceanic wave of modulation
High Rate + Low Depth creates a fast, shimmery Leslie rotary-speaker warble
Recombining dry and modulated signals is mandatory; without the dry signal, the effect becomes pure pitch vibrato

cards.title: Chorus vs. Flanger vs. Vibrato Explained
cards.description: Guitarists often confuse Chorus, Flanger, and Vibrato because all three belong to the time-based modulation family and share identical underlying delay/LFO architectures. Understanding the critical technical differences demystifies their distinct musical roles on your pedalboard.

fields.label: Vibrato (Pitch Only)
fields.value: 100% WET signal only (NO dry signal); pure pitch modulation up and down with no phase cancellation

fields.label: Chorus (Doubler)
fields.value: 50% DRY + 50% WET (5ms–25ms delay); zero feedback regeneration; lush, watery doubling shimmer

fields.label: Flanger (Jet Plane)
fields.value: 50% DRY + 50% WET (ultra-short <5ms delay) WITH high regenerative feedback; metallic swooshing resonance

items: Chorus adds warm, expansive doubling without the dramatic metallic 'jet-plane' whoosh of a flanger
True pitch vibrato sounds moody and sea-sick (used by Lonnie Mack and modern indie indie-pop guitarists)
Many legendary chorus pedals (like the Boss CE-1 and CE-2W) feature dedicated toggle switches for pure vibrato mode

sections.title: Analog BBD Circuits vs. Digital Stereo Algorithms
sections.subtitle: Comparing vintage bucket-brigade compander warmth with pristine multi-voice digital DSP

cards.title: Bucket-Brigade Device (BBD) Warmth
cards.description: Analog chorus pedals use Bucket Brigade Device (BBD) chips (such as the Panasonic MN3007) and companion compander chips (NE570). As analog voltage charges pass across thousands of internal capacitors, clock noise is filtered out with steep analog low-pass filters.

fields.label: Semiconductor Chip
fields.value: Panasonic MN3007 (1024-stage BBD) or MN3207 low-voltage equivalent

fields.label: Tonal Character
fields.value: Warm, organic, slightly dark high-frequency roll-off; sits naturally behind distortion

fields.label: Famous Models
fields.value: Boss CE-1, Boss CE-2, Electro-Harmonix Small Clone

items: Analog companders slightly compress signal peaks, adding musical dynamic sweetness
Naturally blends into guitar solos without the harsh, metallic digital high-end clatter of budget digital units

cards.title: True Spatial Stereo Splitting
cards.description: The acoustic secret of the legendary Roland JC-120 and Boss CE-1. Instead of electronically mixing dry and wet signals into a single mono output, the circuit routes 100% DRY signal to the Left speaker and 100% PITCH VIBRATO to the Right speaker.

fields.label: Left Output
fields.value: 100% unmodulated dry guitar signal

fields.label: Right Output
fields.value: 100% pitch-modulated vibrato signal

fields.label: Acoustic Summing
fields.value: Sound waves cross and mix in the physical air between the two speakers in the room

items: Creates an astonishing, disorienting 3D spatial field that sounds wider than the physical room
Eliminates electronic phase cancellation, preserving 100% of your dry guitar's punch and transient attack
The foundational guitar sound of The Police, The Cure, Cocteau Twins, and 1980s new wave

cards.title: Modern Digital Tri-Chorus & Multi-Voice
cards.description: Pioneered by 1980s studio rack processors (DyTronics / Songbird Tri-Stereo Chorus). Digital DSP runs three independent delay lines simultaneously, each modulated by separate LFOs at different phase angles and rates.

fields.label: Processing Architecture
fields.value: 3 independent digital delay lines (Left, Center, Right) modulated by 3 separate LFOs

fields.label: Tonal Character
fields.value: Ultra-lush, crystalline, dense studio shimmer with zero pitch-wobble seasickness

fields.label: Famous Models
fields.value: TC Electronic Corona Chorus (Tri-Chorus), Strymon Mobius, Eventide ModFactor

items: The iconic clean guitar sound heard on 1980s Los Angeles session records (Michael Landau, Steve Lukather)
Pristine 24-bit audio reproduction delivers sparkling treble chime on acoustic and 12-string guitars

sections.title: Legendary Benchmark Chorus Pedals
sections.subtitle: The industry-standard stompboxes that defined classic rock, new wave, and grunge

cards.title: Boss CE-2W Chorus
cards.description: Crafted in Japan by Boss's Waza Craft custom division. The CE-2W features a 100% all-analog BBD circuit that faithfully recreates both the iconic 1979 CE-2 (warm, subtle analog chorus) and the legendary 1976 CE-1 Chorus Ensemble, complete with true pitch vibrato mode and stereo outputs.

fields.label: Circuit Architecture
fields.value: 100% all-analog bucket-brigade device (BBD) delay line

fields.label: Modes (3 Types)
fields.value: Standard (classic CE-2), CE-1 Chorus (lush JC-120 chorus), and CE-1 Vibrato (true pitch vibrato)

fields.label: Stereo Output
fields.value: Plugging into Output B delivers authentic CE-1 spatial dry/wet stereo splitting

items: The definitive analog chorus pedal chosen by professional studio and touring guitarists worldwide
Adds lush, warm, dimensional body to clean rhythm lines and soaring hard-rock guitar solos
Indestructible Boss compact metal enclosure with silent electronic FET switching

cards.title: Electro-Harmonix Small Clone
cards.description: The classic 1979 analog chorus pedal made famous by Kurt Cobain. Featuring a single large Rate knob and a two-position Depth slide switch, the Small Clone produces a rich, watery, liquid analog chorus that defined the Seattle grunge era.

fields.label: Controls
fields.value: Rate knob (adjusts LFO speed) and Depth switch (toggles between subtle shimmer and deep watery warble)

fields.label: Analog Circuit
fields.value: Discrete BBD analog delay line with compander noise reduction

fields.label: Famous Users
fields.value: Kurt Cobain (Nirvana - 'Come As You Are', 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' solo)

items: The exact watery guitar sound heard on the intro riff and haunting verse of Nirvana's 'Come As You Are'
Setting Depth to high creates a deep, liquid, underwater modulation that flatters drop-tuned alternative rock
Classic heavy-duty folded steel chassis with true hardwire bypass

cards.title: Boss CE-1 Chorus Ensemble
cards.description: Released in 1976, the CE-1 was the very first pedal ever released under the Boss brand name. Housing the exact AC-powered BBD circuitry and discrete analog preamp from the Roland JC-120 amplifier, it is the holy grail of vintage analog modulation.

fields.label: Origin
fields.value: Extracted directly from the 1975 Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus amplifier circuit

fields.label: Analog Preamp
fields.value: Discrete analog input preamp that adds warm, saturated musical overdrive when driven hard

fields.label: Famous Users
fields.value: John Frusciante (Red Hot Chili Peppers), Andy Summers (The Police), Alex Lifeson (Rush)

items: John Frusciante's primary tone-shaping secret: the CE-1's internal preamp colors his entire clean and lead tone
Lush, multi-dimensional chorus with independent foot-switchable True Pitch Vibrato section
Vintage units command thousands of dollars among collectors and top recording studios

sections.title: Versatile Modern Stompboxes & Modulators
sections.subtitle: Feature-packed stereo pedals and frequency-tuned chorus processors

cards.title: TC Electronic Corona Chorus
cards.description: A modern digital chorus powerhouse featuring TC Electronic's legendary SCF (Stereo Chorus Flanger) algorithm, a lush Tri-Chorus mode running three stereo delay lines simultaneously, TonePrint customization, and true stereo inputs and outputs.

fields.label: Tri-Chorus Mode
fields.value: Runs 3 stereo choruses simultaneously with offset LFO phases; eliminates pitch seasickness

fields.label: TonePrint Enabled
fields.value: Beam custom artist presets wirelessly into the pedal using your smartphone pickup coil

fields.label: Controls
fields.value: Speed, Depth, Tone (high-frequency damping), and FX Level (wet/dry blend)

items: Tone knob allows taming bright high-end sparkle or adding crystalline sheen to dark humbuckers
Analog dry-through ensures your primary guitar tone never suffers digital latency or conversion loss
True bypass or high-grade buffered bypass selectable via internal dip switches

cards.title: Boss CE-5
cards.description: The Chorus Ensemble engineered for surgical frequency control. Features dual-concentric High and Low filter knobs that allow guitarists to shape the exact frequency bandwidth of the chorused modulation, preventing muddy bass or piercing treble.

fields.label: Filter Knobs
fields.value: Dual concentric High-Filter and Low-Filter knobs carve out the modulated frequency pocket

fields.label: Bass Guitar Optimization
fields.value: Cutting low-filter frequencies keeps sub-150Hz bass punchy and clean while chorusing upper harmonics

fields.label: Stereo Output
fields.value: Main and Stereo outputs produce expansive spatial panning across two amplifiers

items: The favorite chorus pedal of bassists: allows lush chorus on chordal upper frets without muddying the low E string
Efx Level knob allows blending from subtle acoustic doubling to full dramatic swirl
Durable Boss compact chassis engineered for relentless stage durability

cards.title: Roland JC-120
cards.description: The 120-watt stereo solid-state combo amplifier that introduced the chorus effect to the world in 1975. Houses twin 60-watt power amplifiers pushing two 12-inch silver-cone speakers, projecting true spatial acoustic analog chorusing into the room.

fields.label: Power & Speakers
fields.value: 120W Stereo (60W + 60W); 2x 12-inch custom Roland Silver-Cone drivers

fields.label: Spatial Chorus
fields.value: Dry signal through Left speaker, pitch-vibrato through Right speaker; mixes in room air

fields.label: Famous Artists
fields.value: Andy Summers (The Police), Robert Smith (The Cure), Wes Borland, Johnny Marr

items: The pristine clean high-headroom benchmark that launched the 1980s new wave and alternative guitar sound
Accepts stereo pedalboards into its front-panel inputs with breathtaking spatial clarity
Built-in optical vibrato, spring reverb, and low-noise analog effects loop

sections.title: Pedalboard Signal Chain & Mixing Rules
sections.subtitle: Professional placement rules for electric, acoustic, and bass guitars

cards.title: Pre-Dirt vs. Post-Dirt Chorus Placement
cards.description: Where you place your chorus pedal relative to your overdrive and distortion pedals completely alters its musical personality. Neither position is 'wrong', but they produce radically different sonic textures.

fields.label: Post-Dirt Placement (Modern Standard)
fields.value: Dirt → CHORUS → Amp: Produces wide, polished, pristine 1980s studio sheen with maximum stereo spread

fields.label: Pre-Dirt Placement (Vintage 1970s)
fields.value: CHORUS → Dirt → Amp: The modulated signal hits the distortion circuit, producing chewing, lo-fi, psychedelic grit

fields.label: High-Gain Solos
fields.value: Post-dirt chorus adds massive width to high-gain leads without causing chaotic intermodulation fizz

items: Use Post-Dirt for pristine clean funk, 80s new wave arpeggios, and stadium rock guitar solos
Use Pre-Dirt for raw, vintage, dirty psych-rock textures reminiscent of Jimi Hendrix and early Rush
In amplifiers with high-gain preamp distortion, place chorus in the amplifier's Effects Loop for clean, uncompressed modulation

cards.title: Dialing in Chorus for Bass & Acoustic Guitars
cards.description: Chorus is one of the most effective modulation tools for bassists and acoustic players, but requires careful EQ management to prevent phase cancellation from weakening low-end punch or inducing acoustic feedback.

fields.label: Bass Guitar Optimization
fields.value: Use a pedal with a low-filter control (like Boss CE-5 or CEB-3) to ensure low E and A strings remain dry and punchy

fields.label: Acoustic 12-String Emulation
fields.value: Setting low Depth and moderate Rate on an acoustic guitar simulates the natural microtonal chorus of a 12-string guitar

fields.label: Level Matching
fields.value: Keep Mix around 30%–40% on acoustic instruments to add air and sparkle without artificial seasick wobble

items: Duff McKagan (Guns N' Roses) and Peter Hook (Joy Division / New Order) built legendary basslines around chorus pedals
High-pass filtering on bass chorus keeps kick drum and bass lock-in tight while adding vocal sparkle to high fills
Adds dimensional depth to solo acoustic coffeehouse performances without needing a second guitarist
